STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r3.speaker: Ibn Ḥazm and Rūzbihān al-Baqlī
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r3.claim: A small minority, including Ibn Ḥazm and Rūzbihān al-Baqlī, regards Mary as a female prophet because she receives revelation from Gabriel and named Quranic figures are generally prophets.
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r3.anchor: the Andalusian theologian Ibn Ḥazm (d. 456/1064) and the Persian Sufi Rūzbihān al-Baqlī

STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r4.speaker: most Muslim authorities
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r4.claim: Most authorities reject Mary’s prophethood because the Quran does not explicitly call her a prophet and tradition generally holds prophets to be male; she is instead an exceptionally pious woman of the highest rank among women.
STUDYQURAN:19:intro/r4.anchor: most Muslim authorities do not consider Mary a prophet, but rather an exceptionally pious woman with the highest spiritual rank among women

BURSEVI:v5p247/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p247/r1.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v5p247/r1.claim: Christians face east and Jews west because the appointed meeting and Torah’s giving occurred on the mountain’s western side.
BURSEVI:v5p247/r1.anchor: قال الحسن ومن ثمة اتخذ النصارى المشرق قبلة كما اتخذ اليهود المغرب قبلة

BURSEVI:v5p247/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p247/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p247/r2.claim: Mary secluded herself at her aunt Eshaa’s house near the sun; she stayed in the mosque when pure and went to her aunt’s house during menstruation, then came to wash in winter.
BURSEVI:v5p247/r2.anchor: فإذا حاضت تحولت إلى بيت خالتها وإذا طهرت عادت إلى المسجد

BURSEVI:v5p247/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p247/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p247/r3.claim: The screen was a curtain that prevented people from seeing her.
BURSEVI:v5p247/r3.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (رده كه مانع باشد ازديدن)

BURSEVI:v5p247/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p247/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p247/r4.claim: Gabriel appeared as a handsome, bright-faced, curly-haired, beardless young man; he is called spirit because of his subtle spiritual nature and because religion comes alive through him.
BURSEVI:v5p247/r4.anchor: أتاها الملك في صورة آدمي شاب أمرد وضيىء الوجه جعد الشعر

BURSEVI:v5p247/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p247/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p247/r5.claim: Gabriel is called spirit because he is spiritual and subtle and religion is enlivened through him.
BURSEVI:v5p247/r5.anchor: جبريل فإنه كان روحانيا فأطلق عليه الروح للطافته مثله ولأن الدين يحيى به

BURSEVI:v5p247/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p247/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v5p247/r6.claim: Gabriel is literally spirit in his abstract reality and figuratively so in his imaginal form; abstract spirits can assume forms and convey life, explaining the life in the Samiri’s calf from Gabriel’s trace.
BURSEVI:v5p247/r6.anchor: وقال بعض الكبار جبرائيل هو الروح حقيقة باعتبار حقيقته المجردة

BURSEVI:v5p247/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p247/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p247/r7.claim: Another explanation calls Gabriel spirit figuratively as an affectionate term, like telling a beloved person you are my spirit.
BURSEVI:v5p247/r7.anchor: وقيل سماه روحا مجازا محبة له وتقريبا كقولك أنت روحي لمن تحب

BURSEVI:v5p247/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p247/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p247/r8.claim: His complete human form made Mary comfortable enough to hear God’s words and suited his task of breathing life that would produce a human child.
BURSEVI:v5p247/r8.anchor: لتستأنس بكلامه وتتلقى منه ما يلقي إليها من كلماته تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r1.claim: The eastward withdrawal may have been incidental; reports explain Jewish and Christian eastward prayer by Mary's retreat, though others say Christians faced Jerusalem during Jesus's life.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r1.anchor: وكونه شرقيا كان أمرا اتفاقيا وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r2.claim: The proposal that God chose the east because physical sunrise prefigured Jesus as spiritual light is judged far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r2.anchor: وجوز أن يكون اختاره الله تعالى لأنه مطلع الأنوار وقد علم سبحانه أنه حان ظهور النور العيسوي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r3.claim: One account says Mary stayed in the mosque, moved to her aunt's home during menstruation, and returned after purification; Gabriel came while she washed.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r3.anchor: وروي أنه كان موضعها في المسجد فإذا حاضت تحولت إلى بيت خالتها وإذا طهرت عادت إلى المسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r4.speaker: الأكثر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r4.claim: Most exegetes identify God's Spirit as Gabriel; calling him spirit is metaphorical because religion lives by his revelation, and the possessive construction honors him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r4.anchor: أي جبرائيل عليه السلام كما قاله الأكثر وعبر عنه بذلك لأن الدين يحيا به وبوحيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r5.claim: Abu Muslim identifies the Spirit as Jesus from 4:171, but al-Alusi rejects this because the pronoun in tamaththala refers to the angel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r5.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : المراد من الروح عيسى عليه السلام لقوله تعالى ( وروح منه ) وضمير تمثل الآتي للملك وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r6.speaker: أبو حيوة وسهل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r6.claim: They read rūḥanā with fatḥa on rāʾ, still meaning Gabriel as the cause of servants' life and recipient of divine spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p74#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وسهل ( روحنا ) بفتح الراء والمراد به جبريل عليه السلام أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r1.claim: Tamaththala derives from mithāl and means taking on an appearance; basharan sawiyyan is a fully formed, sound human being.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r1.anchor: مشتق من المثال وأصله أن يتكلف أن يكون مثال الشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r2.claim: Some say Gabriel appeared as Yusuf, a relative serving the sanctuary, to make Mary comfortable; the claim that the form was meant to arouse desire is indecent and contradicted by the next verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r2.anchor: وقيل تمثل في صورة قريب لها اسمه يوسف من خدم بيت المقدس وذلك لتستأنس بكلامه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r3.claim: The suggestion that a handsome appearance provoked Mary's desire conflicts with the testimony of her immediate seeking of refuge and her chastity.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r3.anchor: وما قيل من أن ذلك لتهيج شهوتها فتنحدر نطفتها إلى رحمها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r4.speaker: النقاش
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r4.claim: Al-Naqqash mentions a reading with doubled nūn, rūḥunnā, as the name of an angel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p75/r4.anchor: وذكر النقاش أنه قريء ( روحنا ) بتشديد النون اسم ملك من الملائكة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r1.claim: Maryam set up a screen away from her people; Ibn ʿAbbās says it was a curtain, while others say a wall or a mountain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r1.anchor: {فاتخذت} فضربت {من دونهم حجابا} قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: سترا. وقيل: جلست وراء جدار. وقال مقاتل: وراء جبل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r2.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r2.claim: ʿIkrimah relates that Maryam stayed in the mosque, withdrew to her aunt's home during menstruation, then returned; while bathing unclothed she saw Gabriel as a handsome, well-formed young man.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r2.anchor: وقال عكرمة: إن مريم كانت تكون في المسجد فإذا حاضت تحولت إلى بيت خالتها، حتى إذا طهرت عادت إلى المسجد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r3.claim: The Spirit sent to her is Gabriel, who appeared in the form of a well-proportioned human being.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r3.anchor: {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} يعني: جبريل عليه السلام {فتمثل لها بشرا سويا}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r4.claim: One alternative identifies the Spirit as Jesus, who came in human form and caused her pregnancy; the author says Gabriel is the sounder view.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p223/r4.anchor: وقيل: المراد من الروح عيسى عليه السلام، جاء في صورة بشر فحملت به والأول أصح

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:17/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:17/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:17/r1.claim: Mary put a screen between herself and her family; God's spirit appeared to her in the form of a physically sound human being.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:17/r1.anchor: فأرسلنا إليها روحنا فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:17/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:17/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:17/r2.claim: One account says Mary went from the mosque to her aunt's house during menstruation, secluded herself to bathe, and met Gabriel as a smooth-cheeked young man; his speech reassured her, and perhaps aroused desire so that her seminal fluid entered the womb.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:17/r2.anchor: وكانت تتحول من المسجد إلى بيت خالتها إذا حاضت وتعود إليه إذا طهرت

QASHANI:19:16-17/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r3.claim: Her veil is the sanctuary of holiness, barred from the soul's world by the chest, the limit of material faculties' knowledge and travel.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r3.anchor: والحجاب الذي اتخذته من دونهم هو حظيرة القدس الممنوع من أهل عالم النفس بحجاب الصدر

QASHANI:19:16-17/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r4.claim: The Holy Spirit could not be sent until Mary rose through detachment to the holy world.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r4.anchor: وما لم تترق إلى العالم القدسي بالتجرد لم يمكن إرسال روح القدس إليها

QASHANI:19:16-17/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r5.claim: The spirit took a handsome, well-formed human shape to affect and comfort her nature, awakening desire through imagination.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r5.anchor: وإنما تمثل لها بشرا سوي الخلق

QASHANI:19:16-17/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r6.claim: The imagined effect passes into nature and stirs desire, producing a seminal emission and conception in the womb, as in a wet dream.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r6.anchor: ويسري الأثر من الخيال في الطبيعة فتتحرك شهوتها، فتنزل كما يقع في المنام من الاحتلام

QASHANI:19:16-17/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r7.claim: Revelation resembles true dreams for the bodily faculty, which is inactive during revelation as during sleep.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r7.anchor: وقد مر أن الوحي قريب من المنامات الصادقة لهذه القوة البدنية وتعطلها عن أفعالها عنده كما في النوم

QASHANI:19:16-17/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r8.claim: Images of the rational soul, called the heart, and its contact with holy spirits pass through animal and natural souls and affect the body.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r8.anchor: فكل ما يرى في الخيال من الأحوال الواردة على النفس الناطقة

QASHANI:19:16-17/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r9.claim: Natural science compares male semen to rennet and female semen to milk: one contracts while the other receives, with both capacities present in each.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r9.anchor: ثبت في العلوم الطبيعية أن مني الذكر في تكون الولد بمنزلة الأنفحة في الجبن

QASHANI:19:16-17/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r10.claim: The distinction is relative strength in contracting and receiving powers, not exclusive possession of either power.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r10.anchor: بل على معنى أن القوة العاقدة في مني الذكر أقوى والمنعقدة في مني الأنثى أقوى

QASHANI:19:16-17/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r11.claim: For conception, a woman's strong masculine temperament and warm liver make semen from the right kidney hotter than that from the left.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r11.anchor: وكان مزاج كبدها حارا كان المني المنفصل عن كليتها اليمنى أحر كثيرا

QASHANI:19:16-17/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r12.claim: A receptive, strongly retaining womb lets right-kidney semen act as male and left-kidney semen as female, forming the child.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r12.anchor: وكان مزاج الرحم قويا في الإمساك والجذب.

QASHANI:19:16-17/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:16-17/r13.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:16-17/r13.claim: Support from the Holy Spirit can alter temperament and empower bodily faculties beyond measurable proportion.
QASHANI:19:16-17/r13.anchor: خصوصا إذا كانت النفس متأيدة بروح القدس، متقوية،

BIQAI-FULL:v4p526#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p526#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p526#2/r4.claim: Gabriel, a spirit, took visible human form; he appeared well-proportioned and handsome to lessen her fear.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p526#2/r4.anchor: أي تشبح وهو روحاني بصورة الجسماني

DURR-FULL:v5p495/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p495/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p495/r5.claim: Mary's barrier was a mountain between her and her people while God prepared to honor her and announce Jesus.
DURR-FULL:v5p495/r5.anchor: {حجابا} يعني جبلا فكان الجبل بين مجلسها وبين بيت المقدس

DURR-FULL:v5p495/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p495/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p495/r6.claim: “Our Spirit” is Gabriel, who appeared in a human form.
DURR-FULL:v5p495/r6.anchor: {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} يعني جبريل {فتمثل لها بشرا} في صورة الآدميين

DURR-FULL:v5p495/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p495/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p495/r7.claim: Gabriel's appearance was upright, youthful, fair-faced, tightly curled-haired, with a first trace of moustache.
DURR-FULL:v5p495/r7.anchor: {سويا} يعني معتدلا شابا أبيض الوجه جعدا قططا حين اخضر شاربه

DURR-FULL:v5p499/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Umar Christians use screens at altars and ritual sites because Mary took a screen from her people.
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال لعمر بن الخطاب لم أستحب النصارى الحجب على مذابحهم

DURR-FULL:v5p499/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r2.claim: Abu Salih says God's Spirit was an angel who breathed into Mary's garment and the breath entered her vulva.
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r2.anchor: عن أبي صالح رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} قال: بعث الله إليها ملكا فنفخ في جيبها

DURR-FULL:v5p499/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r3.claim: Qatada identifies God's Spirit sent to Mary as Gabriel.
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} قال: جبريل

DURR-FULL:v5p499/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Gabriel breathed through Mary's robe and the breath reached where God willed.
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} الآية قال: نفخ جبريل في درعها

DURR-FULL:v5p499/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r6.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b says Jesus's spirit appeared as human; Mary conceived when the spirit who spoke to her entered her mouth.
DURR-FULL:v5p499/r6.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب في قوله: {فتمثل لها بشرا سويا} قال: تمثل لها روح عيسى في صورة بشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p80/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p80/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p80/r1.claim: Mary may have made the screen to bathe or to comb her hair.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p80/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p80/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p80/r2.claim: The Spirit is an angel, inferred from God's sending him and the divine possessive; his human appearance was an assumed likeness, not his original form, and بشر is a circumstantial simile meaning a complete human form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p80/r2.anchor: والروح : الملك ، لأن تعليق الإرسال به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r6.claim: The screen was a barrier for worship; al-Suddi says wall, another view says clothing, and some place Mary east of the prayer chamber.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r6.anchor: هي اتخذته لتستتر به عن الناس لعبادتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports two views: the spirit was Gabriel or Jesus; on the latter view an angel appeared to Mary.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r8.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r8.claim: Al-Naqqash says a reading with doubled nun makes ruhana the name of an angel; Ibn Atiyya has not seen this reading elsewhere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r8.anchor: قال النقاش ومن قرأ «روحنا» مشددة النون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r9.claim: Mary’s prophethood is disputed: some infer it from the angelic mission and conversation, while others say she saw an angel in human form; Ibn Atiyya finds prophethood stronger.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p8#2/r9.anchor: واختلف الناس في نبوة مريم فقيل كانت نبية بهذا الإرسال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r1.claim: The screen was a barrier separating Maryam from her family.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r1.anchor: من دونهم يعني أهلها حجابا أي سترا وحاجزا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r2.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r2.claim: One view says she put up a curtain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r2.anchor: أحدها أنها ضربت شترا قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r3.claim: Another view says the sun shaded her so no one could see her.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r3.anchor: ان الشمس أظلتها فلم يرها أحد منهم وذلك مما سترها الله به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r4.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r4.claim: A third view says she made a screen out of walls.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r4.anchor: أنها اتخذت حجابا من الجدران قاله السدي عن أشياخه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r5.claim: One explanation for her seclusion is that she wanted to purify herself after menstruation and comb her hair.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r5.anchor: انفردت لتطهر من الحيض وتمتشط قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r6.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r6.claim: Another explanation is that she went aside to comb lice from her head.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r7.claim: Most authorities identify God's Spirit as Gabriel; Ibn al-Anbari calls him the bearer of God's spirit and relates spirit to breath and joy, while it can also mean revelation and Gabriel its bearer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r7.anchor: فأرسلنا اليها روحنا وهو جبريل في قول الجمهور وقال ابن الأنباري صاحب روحنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r8.claim: Three accounts place Gabriel's arrival while she bathed, after bathing and dressing, or after she entered her house.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r8.anchor: وفي وقت مجيئه اليها ثلاثة أقوال أحدها وهي تغتسل والثاني بعد فراغها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج والماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r9.claim: They report that Spirit could mean the spirit from which Jesus was created, as also implied by Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's account; Ibn al-Anbari finds this unlikely because Gabriel appeared as a fully formed human.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r9.anchor: وقد قيل المراد بالروح هاهنا الروح الذي خلق منه عيسى حكاه الزجاج والماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r10.claim: Gabriel appeared as a fair-faced young man with tightly curled hair and the beginning of a mustache.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r10.anchor: جاءها في صورة شاب أبيض الوجه جعد قطط حين طر شاربه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r11.speaker: أبو نهيك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r11.claim: He reads rūḥan with fatḥa on the rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p216#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو نهيك فأرسلنا اليها روحنا بفتح الراء

SULAMI:v1p423#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p423#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p423#4/r1.claim: God's Spirit is a light cast upon Mary and a special gift to her; from the radiance and effects of this light Jesus, the Spirit of God, emerged.
SULAMI:v1p423#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : نورا منا ألقيناه عليها وخصصناها به فأثرا النور فيه أثره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r5.claim: Mary screened herself from her people; God sent Gabriel, who appeared as a complete, well-formed human.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r5.anchor: وقوله: {فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا} أي: استترت منهم وتوارت، فأرسل الله تعالى إليها جبريل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r6.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وقتادة وابن جريج ووهب بن منبه والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r6.claim: These authorities identify God's Spirit as Gabriel; Ibn Kathir says this is the apparent Qur'anic meaning and links it to the Spirit's descent upon Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد، والضحاك، وقتادة، وابن جريج (12) ووهب بن منبه، والسدي، في قوله: {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} يعني: جبريل،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r7.claim: A report from Ubayy via Abu al-Aliyah says the spirit was Jesus' soul from those pledged at Adam's time, appearing as a man and entering Mary's mouth; Ibn Kathir calls it strange, objectionable, and seemingly Israelite.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p219/r7.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال: إن روح عيسى، عليه السلام، من جملة الأرواح التي أخذ عليها العهد في زمان آدم،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r4.claim: The angel appeared during her ritual washing as a handsome, beardless young man with a complete, well-proportioned human form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r4.anchor: فبينا هي في مغتسلها أتاها الملك في صورة آدمي شاب أمرد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r5.claim: He appeared as a human so she would feel at ease speaking and would not recoil; an angelic appearance would have frightened her and prevented her hearing him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r5.anchor: وإنما مثل لها في صورة الإنسان لتستأنس بكلامه ولا تنفر عنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r6.claim: Her seeking refuge from such a beautiful figure demonstrates chastity and piety; the appearance tested her chastity.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r6.anchor: ودل على عفافها وورعها أنها تعوذت بالله من تلك الصورة الجميلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r8.claim: A further account says the angel stood before her as a servant of the sanctuary named Yusuf, a peer of hers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r8.anchor: وقيل : قام بين يديها في صورة ترب لها اسمه يوسف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r10.claim: The Spirit is Gabriel, since religion is brought to life through him and revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r10.anchor: الروح : جبريل ، لأن الدين يحيا به وبوحيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r11.claim: Alternatively, God calls Gabriel His Spirit metaphorically out of love and honor, as one tells a beloved person, “you are my soul.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r11.anchor: أو سماه الله روحه على المجاز محبة له وتقريبا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r12.speaker: أبو حيوة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p10#3/r12.claim: Abu Haywah reads rūḥanā with fatḥ, because Gabriel is a cause of spiritual life and of receiving the promised spirit in 56:89; it can also mean one whom God draws near.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r7.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r7.claim: The screen Mary made may have been a wall.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r7.anchor: أحدها : حجابا من الجدران ، قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r8.claim: The screen may have been shade that God made to protect her from the sun.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r8.anchor: الثاني : حجابا من الشمس جعله الله ساترا , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r9.claim: The screen may have been from people, as she sought solitude for worship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r9.anchor: الثالث : حجابا من الناس , وهو محتمل , وفيه وجهان : أحدهما : أنها اتخذت مكانا تنفرد فيه للعبادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r10.claim: Alternatively, she withdrew behind a screen to be apart during menstruation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r10.anchor: الثاني : أنها اتخذت مكانا تعتزل فيه أيام حيضها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r11.claim: The spirit sent to Mary may mean the spirit from which the Messiah was created.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r11.anchor: أحدهما : يعني الروح التي خلق منها المسيح حتى تمثل لها بشرا سويا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r12.speaker: الحسن وقتادة والسدي وابن جريج وابن منبه
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r12.claim: The spirit sent to Mary is Gabriel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r12.anchor: الثاني : أنه جبريل , قاله الحسن وقتادة , والسدي , وابن جريج , وابن منبه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r13.claim: Gabriel is called spirit because he is spiritual, an honorific description.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r13.anchor: أحدهما : لأنه روحاني لا يشوبه شيء غير الروح , وأضافه إليه بهذه الصفة تشريفا له .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r14.claim: He is also called spirit because life is brought to souls through him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r15.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r15.claim: One account says Gabriel breathed into the opening and sleeve of Mary's dress, whereupon she conceived.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r15.anchor: أحدهما : أن جبريل نفخ في جيب درعها وكمها فحملت , قاله ابن جريج , منه قول أميه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r16.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r16.claim: Umayya's poem describes Gabriel blowing into the neckline and a well-formed child being born alone, supporting the account of conception.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p361/r16.anchor: فأهوى لها بالنفخ في جيب درعها … فألقت سوي الخلق ليس بتوأم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r1.claim: An alternative account says Mary conceived and delivered in a single episode.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r1.anchor: الثاني : أنه ما كان إلا أن حملت فولدته , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r2.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r2.claim: One account says Mary's pregnancy lasted nine months.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r3.speaker: أبو القاسم الصيمري
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r3.claim: Al-Qasim al-Saymari also reports a nine-month pregnancy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r3.anchor: الثاني : تسعة أشهر . حكى لي ذلك أبو القاسم الصيمري .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r4.claim: A further view says the pregnancy lasted one day.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r5.claim: Another view says it lasted eight months, and that Jesus alone among children born at eight months survived, as a sign.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p362/r5.anchor: الرابع : ثمانية أشهر , وكان هذا آية عيسى فإنه لم يعش مولودا لثمانية أشهر سواه .

FARRA:v2p162/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p162/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p162/r6.claim: Mary would put up a screen when her menstruation began.
FARRA:v2p162/r6.anchor:
وقوله. فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا
[17] كانت إذا أتاها الحيض ضربت حجابا.

MUQATIL:19:16-18/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:16-18/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:16-18/r3.claim: Mary put a mountain between herself and her family so they could not see her; hijāb likewise means the mountain that hides the sun, a year's journey from Mount Qaf.
MUQATIL:19:16-18/r3.anchor: يعني جبلا، فجعلت الجبل بينها وبينهم، فلم يرها أحد منهم، كقوله في ص:

MUQATIL:19:16-18/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:16-18/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:16-18/r4.claim: The Spirit was Gabriel, who appeared as a well-formed human, a smooth-faced young man with curly hair.
MUQATIL:19:16-18/r4.anchor: يعني إنسانا سويا، يعني سوى الخلق، على صور شاب أمرد، جعد الرأس.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r1.claim: Mary made a screen between herself and her family to conceal herself while washing.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r1.anchor: جعلت بينها وبين أهلها حجابا يسترها لتغتسل وراءه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r2.claim: The Spirit is Gabriel; the possessive addition honors him, and he is called Spirit because religion lives through him and revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r2.anchor: جبريل عليه السلام والإضافة للتشريف وإنما سمي روحا لأن الدين يحيا به وبوحيه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r3.claim: Gabriel appeared as a well-proportioned human, a handsome, beardless young man with curly hair.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r3.anchor: أي فتمثل لها جبريل في صورة آدمي شاب أمرد وضئ الوجه جعد الشعر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r4.claim: He took human form so Mary would feel at ease and hear him; an angelic appearance would have frightened her and prevented her from listening.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p33/r4.anchor: وإنما مثل لها في صورة الإنسان لتستأنس بكلامه ولا تنفر عنه ولو بدالها في صورة الملائكة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r8.claim: Some take Our Spirit as Jesus’s spirit, created before bodies and placed in the body God formed in Mary’s womb.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r8.anchor: قيل: هو روح عيسى عليه السلام لأن الله تعالى خلق الأرواح قبل الأجساد

QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r9.claim: Others identify the Spirit as Gabriel; the divine possessive marks honor, and the following description makes Gabriel the apparent referent.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو جبريل وأضيف الروح إلى الله تعالى تخصيصا وكرامة. والظاهر أنه جبريل

QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r10.claim: The angel appeared in human form with sound proportions because Mary could not bear to see Gabriel in his actual form.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:16-18/r10.anchor: سويا } أي مستوي الخلقة لأنها لم تكن لتطيق أو تنظر جبريل في صورته

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#2/r4.claim: The screen was more likely a curtain between Mary and her family than a wall or other barrier.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#2/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أنها جعلت بين نفسها وبينهم سترا وهذا الوجه الثاني أظهر

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r2.claim: Most commentators identify the spirit sent to Mary as Gabriel.

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r3.claim: Abū Muslim identifies the spirit as the spirit that took human form in Mary's womb.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r3.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم إنه الروح الذي تصور في بطنها بشرا

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r4.claim: Razi prefers Gabriel: Gabriel is called Spirit elsewhere, and the later declaration that he is the Lord's messenger who will grant a boy fits him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r4.anchor: والأول أقرب لأن جبريل عليه السلام يسمى روحا

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r5.claim: The name Spirit may reflect his spiritual nature, creation from spirit, reviving religion, or God's affectionate attribution; Abū Ḥaywa's fatḥ reading can evoke the breath and spiritual life promised to the near ones.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r5.anchor: وسمي روحا لأنه روحاني وقيل خلق من الروح وقيل لأن الدين يحيا به

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r6.speaker: أبو حيوة
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r6.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads rūḥan with fatḥ, connecting Gabriel with the life-breath of worshippers or with the promised spirit of the near ones.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة روحنا بالفتح لأنه سبب لما فيه روح العباد

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r7.claim: One view says Gabriel appeared as a handsome, beardless young man; another says he looked like Mary's contemporary, a temple servant named Yusuf; the text does not decide between them.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r7.anchor: ظهر لها على صورة شاب أمرد حسن الوجه سوي الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r8.claim: Gabriel appeared human so Mary could converse without fear; an angelic appearance might have frightened her and prevented her hearing him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r8.anchor: وإنما تمثل لها في صورة الإنسان لتستأنس بكلامه ولا تنفر عنه

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r9.claim: A first objection says that if angels or jinn can assume a known person's form, one cannot be sure today's observed person is the one seen yesterday, inviting skepticism.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r9.anchor: لا يمكننا القطع بأن هذا الشخص الذي أراه في الحال هو زيد الذي رأيته بالأمس

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r10.claim: Razi answers that such doubt also follows from belief in a freely acting Creator able to make an exact duplicate, or from extraordinary planetary conjunctions posited by naturalists.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r10.anchor: ذلك التجويز لازم على الكل لأن من اعترف بافتقار العالم إلى الصانع المختار

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r11.claim: A second objection asks how Gabriel's enormous body could become human-sized: loss of parts would destroy him, while overlapping parts is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r11.anchor: ذلك الشخص العظيم كيف صار بدنه في مقدار جثة الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r12.claim: Razi answers that a bodily Gabriel may have few essential parts and many additional ones, or, if spiritual, may assume large or small forms without difficulty.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r12.anchor: له أجزاء أصلية وأجزاء فاضلة والأجزاء الأصلية قليلة جدا

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r13.claim: A third objection says that allowing Gabriel to take human form would also allow forms as small as insects, an absurd result.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r13.anchor: فلم لا يجوز تمثله في صورة جسم أصغر من الآدمي حتى الذباب

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r14.claim: A fourth objection says assuming forms could undermine mass-transmitted reports, for example by making the person at Badr someone disguised as Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r14.anchor: أن تجويزه يفضي إلى القدح في خبر التواتر

RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r15.claim: Razi says reason allows such forms in principle; reliable transmitted revelation establishes that the insect-like and report-undermining possibilities do not occur.
RAZI-FULL:v21p167#3/r15.anchor: أصل التجويز قائم في العقل وإنما عرف فساده بدلائل السمع

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r67.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r67.speaker: Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r67.claim: The veil may have been a curtain or wall shielding Mary, perhaps while she purified herself.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r67.anchor: a curtain or wall that shielded her from view (Ṭ, Z), perhaps while she was purifying herself (R).

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r68.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r68.speaker: IK, R, Ṭs, Z
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r68.claim: Most commentators identify Our Spirit as Gabriel, also called the Holy Spirit and Trustworthy Spirit.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r68.anchor: Our Spirit is considered by most to be the Archangel Gabriel

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r69.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r69.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r69.claim: Gabriel may be called Spirit because religion is revived through him, as spirit is associated with life.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r69.anchor: perhaps because religion is “revived” through him (Z), as spirit is also associated strongly with the giving of life

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r70.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r70.speaker: Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r70.claim: The angel appeared as a beautiful, radiant, proportioned, blemish-free young man, perhaps to avoid frightening Mary.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r70.anchor: a young, beardless man, beautiful and radiant in appearance, perfectly proportioned (Ṭ, Z)

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r71.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r71.speaker: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r71.claim: Ubayy interpreted both the Spirit and the perfect man as references to Jesus’ spirit.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r71.anchor: considered the Spirit and the perfect man references to the spirit of Jesus

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r72.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r72.speaker: R, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r72.claim: A similar interpretation identifies the Spirit and man with Jesus but is not attributed to Ubayy.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r72.anchor: for a similar interpretation that is not attributed to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb

NAHHAS:v3p9/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p9/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p9/r3.claim: The spirit sent to Mary is Gabriel, called spirit because revelation gives life to servants, as Jesus is also called spirit.
NAHHAS:v3p9/r3.anchor: وهو جبرئيل عليه السلام سمي روحا لأنه يأتي بما يحيا به العباد

NAHHAS:v3p9/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p9/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p9/r4.claim: بشرا سويا is a circumstantial accusative.
NAHHAS:v3p9/r4.anchor: ( فتمثل لها بشرا سويا ) على الحال

TAB-FULL:v15p483/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p483/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p483/r1.claim: Intabadhat means Mary withdrew from her people; the verb is form VIII of n-b-dh, 'to cast aside.'
TAB-FULL:v15p483/r1.anchor: حين اعتزلت من أهلها، وانفردت عنهم، وهو افتعل من النبذ

TAB-FULL:v15p485/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p485/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p485/r1.claim: Mary made a screen between herself and her family and other people.
TAB-FULL:v15p485/r1.anchor: عن السدي، {فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا} [مريم: 17] من الجدران

TAB-FULL:v15p485/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p485/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p485/r3.claim: He says the screen consisted of walls.
TAB-FULL:v15p485/r3.anchor: عن السدي، {فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا} [مريم: 17] من الجدران

TAB-FULL:v15p486/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r1.claim: The spirit sent to Mary was Gabriel.
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} [مريم: 17] قال: أرسل إليها فيما ذكر لنا جبريل

TAB-FULL:v15p486/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r2.claim: He says Gabriel was sent to Mary.
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} [مريم: 17] قال: أرسل إليها فيما ذكر لنا جبريل

TAB-FULL:v15p486/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r3.claim: He says Gabriel appeared to Mary in human form, well proportioned.
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r3.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه، قال: وجدت عندها جبريل قد مثله الله بشرا سويا

TAB-FULL:v15p486/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r4.claim: He identifies the sent spirit as Gabriel.
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} [مريم: 17] قال: جبريل

TAB-FULL:v15p486/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r5.claim: After Mary became pure from menstruation, she found a man with her; Gabriel appeared in a balanced human form.
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r5.anchor: عن السدي، قال: فلما طهرت، يعني مريم من حيضها، إذا هي برجل معها

TAB-FULL:v15p486/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r6.claim: Tamaththala means Gabriel took the appearance of a properly proportioned human being, a man from humankind.
TAB-FULL:v15p486/r6.anchor: فتشبه لها في صورة آدمي سوي الخلق منهم، يعني في صورة رجل من بني آدم

TABATABAI:19:16-17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-17/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-17/r5.claim: The screen separated Mary from her family so she could withdraw for worship, as suggested by the account of Zechariah finding provision with her in the sanctuary.
TABATABAI:19:16-17/r5.anchor: وكأنها اتخذت الحجاب من دون أهلها لتنقطع عنهم

TABATABAI:19:16-17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-17/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-17/r6.claim: A reported detail says Mary left the mosque during menstruation, stayed at Zechariah's house, and Gabriel entered as a handsome, hairless young man; the wording does not support this detail.
TABATABAI:19:16-17/r6.anchor: لا دليل على هذا التفصيل من جهة اللفظ

TABATABAI:19:16-17/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-17/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-17/r7.claim: The spirit is the subject of “appeared”: Gabriel became visible to Mary's perception as a human while remaining a spirit and angel, not actually changing form.
TABATABAI:19:16-17/r7.anchor: فالروح المرسل إليها هو المتمثل لها بشرا سويا

TABATABAI:19:17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:17/r1.claim: The Qur'an's names for the revelation angel—Gabriel, the Holy Spirit, the faithful Spirit, and a noble messenger—identify the spirit sent to Mary as Gabriel.
TABATABAI:19:17/r1.anchor: من كان عدوا لجبريل فإنه نزله على قلبك

TABATABAI:19:17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:17/r2.claim: The angelic announcement to Mary in Ali Imran shows Gabriel's speech is attributed to angels collectively; one person's statement can represent a group sharing a kind or custom.
TABATABAI:19:17/r2.anchor: ونسبة قول جبريل إلى الملائكة من قبيل نسبة قول الواحد من القوم

TABATABAI:19:17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:17/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:17/r3.claim: Calling Gabriel “Our spirit” honors and magnifies him; the author discussed the meaning of spirit under another verse.

TABATABAI:19:17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:17/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:17/r4.claim: The interpretation that the spirit is Jesus and the pronoun in “appeared” refers to Gabriel is mistaken.
TABATABAI:19:17/r4.anchor: إن المراد بالروح في الآية عيسى عليه السلام وضمير تمثل عائد على جبريل

TABATABAI:19:17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:17/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:17/r5.claim: A variant that doubles the nūn in “Our spirit,” making it an angel distinct from Gabriel, is also unacceptable.
TABATABAI:19:17/r5.anchor: بتشديد النون على أن روحنا اسم الملك الذي أرسل إلى مريم

TABATABAI:19:17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:17/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:17/r6.claim: The Qur'an uses appearing only in Mary's story; its context proves Gabriel remained an angel in himself and only appeared in human form to her perception.
TABATABAI:19:17/r6.anchor: باقيا على ملكيته ولم يصر بذلك بشرا

TABATABAI:19:17/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:17/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:17/r7.claim: Linguistically, appearing as something means presenting that form to an observer while remaining oneself, not actually changing species or substance.
TABATABAI:19:17/r7.anchor: ظهوره لها في صورة بشر وليس عليها في نفسه

TABATABAI:19:16-40/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r1.speaker: المفسرون في التفسير الكبير وغيره
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r1.claim: The first objection asks how huge-bodied Gabriel could become human-sized without losing excess parts or causing impossible bodily overlap.
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r1.anchor: فمتى صار في مقدار جثة الإنسان فإن تساقطت أجزاؤه الزائدة

TABATABAI:19:16-40/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r2.speaker: المفسرون في التفسير الكبير وغيره
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r2.claim: The second objection says manifestation would destroy certainty that the person seen today is the same Zayd seen yesterday.
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r2.anchor: امتنع القطع بأن هذا الشخص الذي يرى الآن هو زيد

TABATABAI:19:16-40/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r3.speaker: المفسرون في التفسير الكبير وغيره
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r3.claim: The third objection argues that an angel's appearance as a person would also permit appearance as insects and other animals, an allegedly false consequence.
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r3.anchor: جاز التمثل بصورة غيره كالبعوض والحشرات وغيرها

TABATABAI:19:16-40/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r4.speaker: المفسرون في التفسير الكبير وغيره
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r4.claim: The fourth objection says manifestation undermines trust in mass-transmitted reports, such as the Prophet's combat at Badr, by allowing an impersonator.
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r4.anchor: ارتفع الوثوق بالخبر المتواتر كخبر مقاتلة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يوم بدر

TABATABAI:19:16-40/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r5.claim: The proposed answer to the bodily-size objection—extra bodily parts or a spirit wearing differently sized bodies—assumes a real transformation that the verse does not describe.
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r5.anchor: وأجيب عن الأول بأنه لا يمتنع أن يكون لجبريل أجزاء أصلية قليلة

TABATABAI:19:16-40/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r6.claim: The context says Gabriel remained an angel and appeared human only within Mary's perception; Satan appeared as Suraqa at Badr, though Suraqa was in Mecca.
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r6.anchor: والآية بسياقها ظاهرة في أن جبريل لم يخرج بالتمثل عن كونه ملكا

TABATABAI:19:16-40/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r7.claim: Reports describe Satan appearing as an old man at the council and as Munabbih ibn al-Hajjaj at the pledge; worldly life, wealth, children, deeds, and dreams also appear in forms.
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r7.anchor: كتمثل إبليس يوم الندوة للمشركين في صورة شيخ كبير

TABATABAI:19:16-40/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r8.claim: Dream figures represent abstract meanings with no independent visible form, so no transformation of an original body is involved.
TABATABAI:19:16-40/r8.anchor: وما ورد من تمثل الأعمال للإنسان في القبر ويوم القيامة

TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r1.claim: A proposed reply says creation of a duplicate Zayd is possible but rare, preserving ordinary certainty; the author says this does not explain how its rarity could be known.
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r1.anchor: ولعله لما كان مثل هذه الحوادث نادرا لم يلزم منه قدح

TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r2.claim: The mistake is assuming sensation directly reaches an external object as it exists; sensation gives an image, while reason and experience judge the external thing.
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r2.anchor: أما الإشكال فهو مبني على أن الذي يناله الحس هو عين المحسوس الخارجي

TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r3.claim: Illusions—size and direction shifts, apparent motion, a distant person seeming tiny, and the sun seeming small—show that sensory images differ from external objects.
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r3.anchor: كمشاهدة الكبير صغيرا والعالي سافلا والمستقيم مائلا والمتحرك ساكنا

TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r4.claim: The sensory image is immediately certain as an experience; claims about the external object arise through thought and examination rather than sensation alone.
TABATABAI:19:16-40#2/r4.anchor: المحسوس لنا بالحقيقة هي الصورة التي في ظرف حسنا

TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r1.claim: Sense organs modify sensation; causes may be external or internal, such as sudden fear creating frightening images, and perception may mistake a mirage for water.
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r1.anchor: أن لجهازات الحواس أنواعا من التصرف في المحسوس

TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r2.claim: A difference between perception and the external object does not destroy trust in sensation; reliability depends on experience and reasoning, especially tested experience.
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r2.anchor: لا تستدعي ارتفاع الوثوق وبطلان الاعتماد على الحس

TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r3.claim: The proposed reply invokes revelation to bar animal forms, but the author finds no reliable scriptural proof; human manifestation does not entail animal manifestation, and bare intellectual possibility is harmless.
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r3.anchor: وفيه أنه لا دليل من جهة السمع يعتد به

TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r4.claim: The proposed answer to the fourth objection relies on revelation to secure transmitted reports, but the same uncertainty affects revelation received through hearing; the earlier answer resolves it.
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r4.anchor: وفيه أن نظير الاحتمال قائم في نفس دليل السمع

TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r5.claim: Manifestation presents a thing in a familiar form suited to its purpose: Gabriel appears human because people understand a messenger as someone who speaks to the recipient; worldly life appears as a beautiful woman to allure.
TABATABAI:19:16-40#3/r5.anchor: فظهر مما قدمناه أن التمثل هو ظهور الشيء للإنسان بصورة يألفها الإنسان

TABATABAI:19:18-20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:18-20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:18-20/r1.claim: This account is not sophistry: a real thing may appear through a familiar perceptible image; sophistry instead posits an image with nothing behind it.
TABATABAI:19:18-20/r1.anchor: قلت فرق بين أن يكون هناك حقيقة يظهر للمدرك

TABRISI:19:16-17/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:16-17/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
TABRISI:19:16-17/r8.claim: God’s spirit sent to Mary is Gabriel; calling him spirit honors his spiritual nature and the possessive relation to God.
TABRISI:19:16-17/r8.anchor: يعني جبرائيل ع عن ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة وغيرهم

TABRISI:19:16-17/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:16-17/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:19:16-17/r9.claim: Abu Muslim says the spirit from which Christ was created appeared to Mary as a human; the author prefers Gabriel, citing the exegetes’ agreement.
TABRISI:19:16-17/r9.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم إن الروح الذي خلق منه المسيح تصور لها إنسان

THALABI:v6p209/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p209/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p209/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Mary's ḥijāb was a screen; Muqatil says she placed a mountain between herself and her people.
THALABI:v6p209/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: سترا، قال مقاتل: جعلت الجبل بينها وبين قومها،

THALABI:v6p209/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p209/r3.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v6p209/r3.claim: Ikrima says Mary stayed in the mosque when pure and went to her aunt's house during menstruation; while washing, she encountered Gabriel as a handsome, smooth-faced young man.
THALABI:v6p209/r3.anchor: قال عكرمة: إن مريم كانت تكون في المسجد ما دامت طاهرا، فإذا حاضت تحولت إلى بيت خالتها

THALABI:v6p209/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p209/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p209/r4.claim: The spirit sent to Mary is Gabriel, or the spirit of Jesus by an honorific attribution.
THALABI:v6p209/r4.anchor: فذلك قوله فأرسلنا إليها روحنا يعني جبرئيل (عليه السلام) وقيل: روح عيسى ابن مريم

THALABI:v6p209/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p209/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p209/r5.claim: Gabriel appeared fully human so Mary could remain composed and hear him; his true form would have frightened her and prevented her from listening.
THALABI:v6p209/r5.anchor: لم ينقص منه شيء وإنما أرسله في صورة البشر لتثبت مريم عليها السلام وتقدر على استماع كلامه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r1.claim: Maryam put a barrier between herself and her family so they could not see her.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r1.anchor: {فاتخذت من دونهم} أي من دون أهلها لئلا يرونها {حجابا} سترا حاجزا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r2.claim: He identifies the barrier as a mountain between Maryam and the people; Muqatil links the same word to the barrier in the account of Solomon.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r2.anchor: يريد جعلت الجبل بينها وبين الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r3.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r3.claim: He says the barrier was made of walls.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r3.anchor: السدي: (حجابا من الجدران) (¬6). {فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} قال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r4.claim: While Maryam was bathing after menstruation, Gabriel appeared to her as a handsome, beardless young man.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r4.anchor: المفسرون: (بينما هي تغتسل من الحيض إذ عرض لها جبريل -عليه السلام-

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r5.claim: The spirit sent to Maryam is Gabriel; تمثل means taking shape and resembling, and the resulting human form was complete and proportionate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p213/r5.anchor: إليها روحنا} يعني جبريل {فتمثل} فتصور وتشبه {لها بشرا سويا} معتدلا تاما.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:17-18/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:17-18/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:17-18/r1.claim: Mary screened herself from her people; God's spirit is Gabriel, who appeared as a fully formed human.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:17-18/r1.anchor: تتستر به عنهم { فأرسلنا إليها روحنا } جبريل عليه السلام

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r1.claim: The “Spirit” sent to Mary was Gabriel.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r1.anchor: {من أهلها مكانا شرقيا {16} فاتخذت من دونهم حجابا فأرسلنا إليها روحنا} [مريم: 16-17] يعني جبريل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r2.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says Gabriel appeared to Mary as a perfectly formed human in human form and appearance.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r2.anchor:
{فتمثل لها بشرا سويا} [مريم: 17] يعني سوي الخلق، بشرا في صورة البشر وخلقهم.
تفسير السدي.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r3.claim: Qatāda reports that Gabriel was sent to Mary in the form of Adam.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r3.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: أرسل إليها فيما يذكر جبريل في صورة آدم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī recounts that Zakariyya cared for Mary; during menstruation he moved her from the prayer chamber to his home with her sister, then returned her there when she was purified. Once, after washing, she sat in the eastern room behind a hanging screen, where Gabriel came to her.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p218#2/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كان زكرياء كفل مريم وكانت أختها تحته، وكانت تكون في المحراب

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:16/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:16/r2.speaker: tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:16/r2.claim: Commentators identify the sent spirit as Gabriel; unable to perceive the angel in his true form, Mary saw him as a well-formed man, feared harm, then asked how a virgin could bear a child.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:16/r2.anchor: Müfessirler 17. âyette Allah tarafından gönderildiği bildirilen “ruh”un Cebrâil olduğu kanaatindedirler

SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r1.claim: The majority read rūḥanā with ḍamma and understand it as that by which people live.
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r1.anchor: والجمهور على ضم الراء من " روحنا " وهو ما يحيون به.

SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r2.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r2.claim: Abu Haywa and Sahl read the word with fatḥa, meaning something that brings relief to servants, compared with 56:89.
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وسهل بفتحها، أي: ما فيه راحة للعباد

SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r3.speaker: النقاش
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r3.claim: Al-Naqqash reports a reading with doubled nūn and says it names an angel.
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r3.anchor: وحكى النقاش أنه قد قرئ " روحنا " بتشديد النون، وقال

SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r4.claim: Basharan sawiyyan is a circumstantial accusative of the subject of tamaththala; the indefinite noun can serve as a ḥāl because it is described.
SAMIN-DURR:19:17/r4.anchor: قوله: { بشرا سويا } حال من فاعل " تمثل ". وسوغ وقوع الحال

ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r3.claim: One report says Mary went east because she wanted to bathe after menstruation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r3.anchor: قيل إنها - قصدت نحو مطلع الشمس، لأنها أرادت الغسل من الحيض.

ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r4.claim: The Spirit is Gabriel, as shown by his appearing to Mary as a well-formed man.
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r4.anchor: ويدل على أن جبريل عليه السلام هو الروح قوله: (فتمثل لها بشرا سويا).

ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r5.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r5.claim: Another interpretation identifies the Spirit as Jesus, since he is a spirit from God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r5.anchor: وقيل الروح عيسى، لأنه روح من الله - عز وجل

ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r6.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r6.claim: A further view says the Spirit entered Mary through her mouth.
ZAJJAJ:v3p322/r6.anchor: وقيل إن الروح دخل من في مريم

ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n13/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n13/r1.claim: Mary apparently withdrew to pray and meditate undisturbed.
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n13/r1.anchor: in order to devote herself undisturbed to prayer and meditation

ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n13/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n13/r2.speaker: Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n13/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir suggests the eastern place may have been a Temple chamber where Mary's mother had dedicated her to service.
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n13/r2.anchor: as Ibn Kathir suggests, signify an eastern chamber of the Temple, to the service of which Mary had been dedicated by her mother

ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r1.claim: Ruh often means divine inspiration, but can also denote the angel or spiritual medium through which inspiration reaches God's elect; here it refers to the angel of revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r1.anchor: the term ruh often denotes "divine inspiration". Occasionally, however, it is used to describe the medium through which such inspiration is imparted

ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r2.claim: Because mortals cannot see an angel in its true form, God made the angel appear to Mary as a well-made human being.
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r2.anchor: mortals cannot perceive an angel in his true manifestation, God caused him to appear to Mary "in the shape of a well-made human being"

ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r3.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r3.claim: Razi understands the angel's designation as ruh to indicate that angels are purely spiritual beings without a physical element.
ASAD-NOTES:19:16#n14/r3.anchor: the designation of the angel as ruh ("spirit" or "soul") indicates that this category of beings is purely spiritual, without any physical element

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: John's story prefaces Jesus' birth and upbringing: as a predecessor and relative with a similar life, he prompts Christians to reconsider why they deify one of two consecutive prophets from the same family.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: By mentioning both of them together, the Almighty has invited the Christians to open their eyes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The barrier reflects Mary's i'tikāf; God tested her by sending an angel in human form, an unusual appearance that confronted her without prior experience of divine communication, and her character was matchless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It seems that God wanted to test her when He sent an angel to her in the form of a human being.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan like the previous one; Muqatil exempts the prostration verse, saying it was revealed in Medina after the migration to Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كالسورة التي قبلها. وقال مقاتل: إلا آية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.claim: The surahs connect through astonishing stories: the earlier tells of the Cave, Moses and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn; this one of John’s birth to an old man and barren woman and Jesus’ birth without a father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى ضمن السورة قبلها قصصا عجبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r8.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says the ḥijāb consisted of walls; another view says clothes, while Ibn ʿAbbās says she screened herself from people with a mountain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r8.anchor: قال السدي: كان من جدران. وقيل: من ثياب. وعن ابن عباس: جعلت الجبل بينها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r9.claim: The apparent divine sending and the angel's conversation with Mary suggest that she was a prophetess.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r9.anchor: وظاهر الإرسال من الله إليها ومحاورة الملك تدل على أنها نبية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r10.claim: Another view denies Mary's prophethood: an angel spoke to her in human form, as Gabriel appeared as Dihya and in the report about Islam and faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: لم تنبأ وإنما كلمها مثال بشر ورؤيتها للملك كما رئي جبريل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r11.claim: The apparent 'Our Spirit' is Gabriel, called spirit because religion lives through his revelation; alternatively the name is affectionate metaphor, or refers to Jesus as in 'a spirit from Him,' with the angel then taking form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن الروح جبريل لأن الدين يحيا به ويوحيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r12.speaker: أبو حيوة وسهل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r12.claim: They read rawḥanā with an open rāʾ, because Gabriel brings life to servants or is near God and promised spirit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وسهل روحنا بفتح الراء لأنه سبب لما فيه روح العباد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r13.speaker: النقاش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r13.claim: Al-Naqqāsh reports a reading with a doubled nūn, making Rawḥannā the name of an angel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r13.anchor: وذكر النقاش أنه قرىء روحنا بتشديد النون اسم ملك من الملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r14.claim: Bushran is an accusative circumstantial description of how the spirit appeared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r14.anchor: وانتصب بشرا سويا على الحال لقوله وأحيانا يتمثل لي الملك رجلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r15.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r15.claim: The angel appeared as a human so Mary would feel familiar with him and could listen rather than be frightened by an angelic form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p247#2/r15.anchor: قيل: وإنما مثل لها في صورة الإنسان لتستأنس بكلامه ولا تنفر عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p248/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p248/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p248/r3.claim: Another says the figure who came to Mary appeared as a familiar temple servant named Yusuf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p248/r3.anchor: وقيل: قام بين يديها في صورة ترب لها اسمه يوسف من خدم بيت المقدس

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r1.claim: The author says Jesus's extraordinary miracle led many followers to deify him, although his mission called people away from worship of humans and toward worship of God alone.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r1.anchor: لكن معجزة المسيح الخارقة، ما لبث أن التبست على كثير من أتباعه، فقالوا بإلوهيته وهو الذي بعث لينسخ عصر الشرك وعبادة البشر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r2.claim: After centuries of disputes about Jesus's nature, God chose Muhammad as the final messenger, fully human and subject to ordinary human feelings and needs.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r2.anchor: بشراً سوياً يأكل الطعام ويمشي في الأسواق، وتجوز عليه أعراض البشرية وعواطفها وهمومها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r3.claim: The author's study centers on the Qur'an as the great sign of Muhammad's prophethood: a clear Arabic book that the Arabs could not match.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r3.anchor: وكانت المعجزة الكبرى الشاهدة على نبوة هذا البشر الرسول، كتاباً عربياً مبيناً يعيى العرب أن يأتوا بمثله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r4.claim: The author rejects the claim that the Muʿtazilites denied all miracles besides the Qur'an: they affirmed other miracles as proofs, but did not rely on reports unseen by later audiences in debate.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r4.anchor: وليس صحيحاً أن المعتزلة أبطلوا سائر المعجزات غير القرآن، فالحق أنهم أثبتوها معجزة ودلالة على النبوة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r5.claim: Islam confirms and safeguards the truth in earlier revelations and completes the prophetic message as humanity reaches a stage able to bear its responsibilities.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p56/r5.anchor: وإذ جاء الإسلام مصدقاً لما بين يديه من رسالات الله ومهيمناً عليها بما نقى من جوهر الدين الحق، اختتمت به الرسالات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p245/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p245/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p245/r5.claim: Ḥijāb is a barrier that prevents perception; a blind person is called screened because something blocks sight.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p245/r5.anchor: الحجاب : الحاجز المانع من الإدراك . ويقال للأعمى : محجوب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p245/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p245/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p245/r7.claim: The second sense is a curtain or screen, as in Mary’s screen from her people and the screen behind which wives are addressed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p245/r7.anchor: والثاني : الستر ، ومنه قوله تعالى في مريم

ITQAN:v4p371#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p371#2/r1.speaker: أبو حيوة
ITQAN:v4p371#2/r1.claim: Abu Haywa reads روحنا with a doubled letter in the phrase.
ITQAN:v4p371#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو حيوة ﴿ فأرسلنا إليها روحنا ﴾ بالتشديد

ITQAN:v4p371#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p371#2/r2.speaker: ابن مهران
ITQAN:v4p371#2/r2.claim: Ibn Mihran interprets روحنا as a proper name for Gabriel.
ITQAN:v4p371#2/r2.anchor: وفسره ابن مهران بأنه اسم لجبريل حكاه الكرماني في عجائبه

ITQAN:v2p414/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p414/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p414/r15.claim: Rūḥ can refer to Gabriel, as in the passages describing God sending His spirit and the trustworthy spirit bringing revelation.
ITQAN:v2p414/r15.anchor: 6 وجبريل ﴿ فأرسلنا إليها روحنا ﴾ ﴿ نزل به الروح الأمين ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p23/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p23/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p23/r1.claim: Ittakhadhat can mean that Mary drew or spread a screen apart from her family.
DAMGHANI:v1p23/r1.anchor: اتخذت أرخت . كقوله تعالى في سورة مريم

DAMGHANI:v1p253/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r7.claim: Sawiyy can describe a well-formed human figure; the related forms also mean that God fashioned a creature's form.
DAMGHANI:v1p253/r7.anchor: السوي في الخلقة وصورة البشر قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r6.claim: A second Quranic sense is Gabriel, called the Holy Spirit, the spirit sent to Mary, the trustworthy spirit, and the spirit descending with the angels.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p352/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p352/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p352/r3.claim: A second sense is well formed in the human shape; examples include the angel appearing as a man and God forming the human being.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p352/r3.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن السوي في القرآن على أربعة أوجه

NASHR:v1p301/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p301/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p301/r2.claim: The text lists fourteen places of Ruways's optional assimilation: three in al-Baqara, then examples in al-Araf, al-Kahf, Maryam, Taha, al-Naml, al-Zumar, al-Rum, al-Shura, al-Najm, and al-Infitar.
NASHR:v1p301/r2.anchor: واختلف عنه أيضا في أربعة عشر حرفا وهي ثلاثة في البقرة فويل للذين يكتبون الكتاب بأيديهم

NASHR:v1p301/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p301/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني وابن الفحام
NASHR:v1p301/r8.claim: Al-Dani and Ibn al-Fahham report Ruways assimilating both fa-tamaththala laha and wa-li-tusnaʿa ʿalayya; al-Tadhkira and al-Mabhaj also list them.
NASHR:v1p301/r8.anchor: وروى أبو عمرو الداني، وابن الفحام إدغام فتمثل لها، ولتصنع على الحرفين كليهما

NASHR:v1p302/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p302/r4.speaker: الباقون عن رويس
NASHR:v1p302/r4.claim: Other transmitters from Ruways show all these passages; both assimilation and clear pronunciation are sound transmissions from him.
NASHR:v1p302/r4.anchor: وروى الباقون عن رويس إظهار جميع ذلك، والوجهان عنه صحيحان
